prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1250; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The policyholder's driver reported a low-speed head-on collision in a parking area and described neck pain at the scene. The driver is named on the policy, and the claimant is not represented by a lawyer.

Entry 2: The police report confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the impact. No independent witnesses have been identified, so the file relies on the parties' accounts and the police findings.

Entry 3: Photos taken at inspection show some details of the collision. The vehicle damage is mostly in line with the described impact, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is known from our records.

Entry 4: A neighbor mentioned seeing the car with damage some weeks before the reported loss. I have noted this statement and will follow up to verify it.

Entry 5: The claimant added a few small details in a recorded follow-up call, but the core account has stayed the same since the first report.

Entry 6: The claimant's neck strain is consistent with the kind and force of the crash. Treatment followed a usual course, and no earlier injury to the same body area is known.

Entry 7: Treatment tapered off as the claimant improved. The file is being reviewed pending final medical notes and the outcome of the neighbor follow-up.
